slides.say: In triangle A B C, A E is the altitude to B C. Point D lies on A E, and D B C is an equilateral triangle. Given: B E is four centimeters, and A D is three root three centimeters. What is the shaded area, in square centimeters?

Shaded areas are quite common on the exam. The main way to handle them is to subtract areas. We ask what the shaded part is made of, or what minus what gives it. [short pause] We'll solve it two ways, by subtracting areas, and then with a shorter insight.
[short pause] Here, take the big triangle A B C, and take away the white triangle D B C. What's left is exactly the shaded part.
at: take the big triangle A B C
the white triangle D B C

slides.say: To find these areas, we first complete the data. B E is four, so E C is four too. Why? D B C is equilateral, and in an equilateral triangle the altitude is also a median. It cuts the base into two equal halves. So B C is eight.
at: so E C is four too

slides.say: Now the altitude D E. Look at the small triangle D E C on the right. The altitude splits the equilateral triangle into two gold triangles, thirty, sixty, ninety. The short leg, opposite the thirty, is E C, four. The other leg is the short leg times root three, so D E is four root three.
at: Look at the small triangle D E C
so D E is four root three

slides.say: And the whole altitude A E is A D plus D E, three root three plus four root three, which is seven root three.

Now the big triangle. Its base B C is eight, and its height A E is seven root three. Eight times seven root three, over two. Eight over two is four, and four times seven root three is twenty-eight root three.
at: Its base B C is eight

slides.say: The white triangle has the same base, eight, and its height D E is four root three. Eight times four root three, over two, is sixteen root three.

There's another way to get the white area, because it's equilateral. The area of an equilateral triangle is its side squared, times root three, over four. Eight squared is sixty-four, and sixty-four over four is sixteen. So again sixteen root three.
at: The area of an equilateral triangle

slides.say: Now subtract. Twenty-eight root three minus sixteen root three is twelve root three. Choice number two is our answer.
at: Choice number two is our answer

slides.say: [pause] There's a shorter way, with an insight. Turn your head a little. The shaded part is two triangles, A D C on the right, and A D B on the left.
at: A D C on the right

slides.say: For the area of A D C we need a base and its height. The base is given, A D, three root three. The height to it, from C, is outside the triangle, because A D C has an obtuse angle at D. We extend the base A D down to E. E C is perpendicular to that line, and E C is four, the same as B E. So the height is four.
at: We extend the base A D

slides.say: Three root three times four, over two, is six root three. That's one shaded triangle. The other one, A D B, is its mirror image, so it's six root three too. Twice six root three is twelve root three, choice number two again, with almost no calculating.
at: The other one, A D B
so it's six root three too

slides.say: Careful, six root three, choice number three, is only one of the two shaded triangles. [pause] Okay. I'll see you in the next question.
at: six root three, choice number three
